title: Case 1: Taxes Not to be Imposed Save by Authority of Law (Article 265 • Writ Petition)
legalTheme: Part XII: Finance, Property, Contracts and Suits • Article 265
factualMatrix: Before the Supreme Court of India (Article 32), an aggrieved petitioner challenged an impugned executive notification and enforcement order issued by the Union Ministry / Central Authority under Article 265 (Taxes Not to be Imposed Save by Authority of Law) of Part XII (Finance, Property, Contracts and Suits). Relying on the core guarantee that Foundational principle of fiscal democracy and rule of law: No tax shall be levied or collected except by authority of a validly enacted, constitutional statute. and citing Union of India v. Mohit Minerals Pvt Ltd (2022), the petitioner sought judicial invalidation for violating constitutional limits and procedural fairness.
framingQuestions: 1. Whether the Writ Petition before the Supreme Court of India (Article 32) is maintainable under Article 265?
2. Does the Union Ministry / Central Authority's executive notification and enforcement order conform to Article 265 (Taxes Not to be Imposed Save by Authority of Law)?
3. How does Union of India v. Mohit Minerals Pvt Ltd (2022) govern the constitutional validity and relief in this matter?
statutoryApplicability: Union of India v. Mohit Minerals Pvt Ltd (2022)
modelAnswer:
1. MAINTAINABILITY: The Writ Petition before the Supreme Court of India (Article 32) is maintainable as it raises a direct constitutional question under Article 265 (Part XII).

2. SUBSTANTIVE ANALYSIS (Article 265): Foundational principle of fiscal democracy and rule of law: No tax shall be levied or collected except by authority of a validly enacted, constitutional statute. Applying the governing principle—'No tax without authority of law (Art 265).'—the impugned executive notification and enforcement order by the Union Ministry / Central Authority must strictly satisfy constitutional bounds.

3. PRECEDENT (Union of India v. Mohit Minerals Pvt Ltd (2022)) & RELIEF: Guided by Union of India v. Mohit Minerals Pvt Ltd (2022), any overreach inconsistent with Article 265 is liable to be quashed or suitably restrained.
